summary: Concurrent healthy journal hooks report cursor contention as unavailable context
evidence: During the final parallel tool polls in this session, three PostToolUse injections reported cursor busy although the holder completed normally and no lock survived. These notices consume model context without identifying damaged evidence.

summary: The campaign proxy prototype reconstructs no budget state after restart
evidence: control/proxy.mjs initializes spent and reserved to zero on every process start despite an existing usage.jsonl; no restart has occurred and the two canaries remain charged in the current process

summary: The native Codex canary ran without lifecycle hooks and borrowed the Claude canary session identity
evidence: Codex thread 01a08c8d-b171-7711-b2b4-85091c668802 created no journal cursor, reported no SessionStart instructions, and wrote d-039b2a2b under Claude session e7c65e68-9364-401c-a7b8-f8341cec95aa after reading the journal. The hook wiring check alone passed. No substantive reviewer has been dispatched.

summary: The campaign controller kills a reviewer after one failed five-second health request, turning a transient monitoring failure into lost review context and incomplete-usage shutdown
evidence: control/run.py launch catches every status exception and immediately docker-kills its client; 38 of 50 result.json records say meter_unavailable. The proxy remains reachable and stopped with liability 107.1270847, far below the 300 USD ceiling. The first upstream abort belongs to a meter_unavailable reviewer; original exception details were not recorded, so the exact trigger remains conjectural.

summary: A full Coherence test run fans out one CLI process per registered command inside two command-policy tests, exceeding the 1 GiB reviewer container and competing with the live agent and meter
evidence: No-inference probe of frozen campaign repo reached 933814272 bytes and 271 tasks in 9.37 seconds. Process tree shows commands.test.ts concurrently parenting dozens of /repo/src/cli.ts command invocations. OrbStack kernel records 1 GiB memory plus 1 GiB swap exhaustion and two killed Claude processes during recovery, before the controller killed the remaining reviewers.

summary: Receipt repository-root check rejects a macOS checkout reached through its /var alias
evidence: New executable receipt fixtures failed with receipt mode requires the repository root: Git resolves /var to /private/var while the caller root retains the alias.

summary: Receipt execution attribution accepts skipped or todo node:test cases as successful execution
evidence: Independent reviewer ran public verify --receipt with test.skip and failing test.todo; receipts reported problems:[] and the verifies edge cleared completed work. The old serial runner accepted an exit-zero TAP row using testMatch, and oracleChecked only meant lookup was attempted.

summary: Receipt inventory silently ignores a renamed surviving start under the temporary publication prefix
evidence: Independent reviewer renamed an incomplete start to .pending-<run UUID>; listReceipts returned an empty inventory. No false verification was granted, but surviving incomplete evidence disappeared.

summary: A recent pre-existing batch report can be attributed to a receipt whose runner executed no tests
evidence: Independent reviewer seeded a passing Vitest JSON report, then ran a script that only exits 1. The old two-second report mtime tolerance accepted it through public verify --receipt with executed:true and no problems.

summary: Receipt execution repair labels a real failed assertion as not executed
evidence: Reviewer reran a named TAP assertion that throws: Node emitted not ok and exit 1, but the receipt stored executed:false because attribution fired only for successful oracle results.

summary: Concurrent status publication scratch bytes can spuriously stale an otherwise unchanged receipt
evidence: Independent paired CLI batch runs produced an after manifest containing only a new .coherence/status-UUID.tmp in addition to the same seven inputs. Status itself already excludes these publication outputs from its own Git reading.
